chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no bail regarding a Penalty (Hadd)'.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.حَدّ: A fixed, mandatory punishment prescribed by Sharia for specific crimes.
key_terms.كَفَالَة: Guarantee or bail; the act of guaranteeing someone's presence or liability.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bail (kafalah) for fixed Islamic penalties (hadd)?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes that 'kafalah' (guarantee) is inapplicable to 'hadd' penalties, reflecting the Shia juristic view that these fixed divine punishments are absolute and not subject to the procedural flexibility allowed for 'ta'zir' (discretionary) penalties. By citing the Prophet directly, al-Kulayni underscores the certainty of the punishment's execution regardless of a guarantor's intervention, a principle widely accepted in Usuli jurisprudence to distinguish between the rigidity of hadd and the negotiability of other legal categories.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘There is no bail regarding a Penalty (Hadd)’.
